name: Nkomo-Lindqvist NL-22 'Peacemaker'
description:
The Nkomo-Lindqvist NL-22 is a semi-automatic pistol chambered in .22 LR, designed as a training weapon and low-threat personal defense option. The frame is lightweight polymer with a full-size grip designed to approximate the dimensions of common duty pistols, allowing new shooters to build muscle memory that transfers to larger weapons. The recoil is negligible, and the report is mild enough to shoot without ear protection in open environments.

Nkomo-Lindqvist is a small South African-Scandinavian partnership that specializes in the training and recreational market — a niche that larger manufacturers consider beneath their attention. The NL-22 is their flagship product, sold in bulk to shooting ranges, security training academies, and civilian firearms education programs throughout the Mids.

The Peacemaker's name is slightly ironic — the .22 LR round is the least threatening caliber available in a semi-automatic pistol, and carrying one for self-defense is generally regarded as only marginally better than carrying nothing. Nonetheless, the NL-22 has a small but devoted following among people who believe that any gun you can shoot accurately is better than a powerful gun you can't.
specifications: caliber: .22 LR effective_range: 25 meters rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic magazine_capacity: 12 rounds weight: 0.38 kg
tactical_use: A training and light personal defense weapon with minimal recoil and report. Not effective against armored or augmented targets. Useful for firearms familiarization and basic marksmanship training. In a defensive scenario, effectiveness depends entirely on shot placement, as the .22 LR round lacks inherent stopping power.
cultural_context: The NL-22 is the first gun many GLMZ residents ever fire. Shooting ranges in the Mids stock them by the dozen. There's a certain nostalgic affection for the weapon among experienced shooters who remember learning on one. As a carry weapon, it draws polite skepticism at best.
known_users: Elderly residents who find larger calibers unmanageable
story_hooks: A fatal shooting with a .22 LR round that penetrated military-grade body armor — impossible with standard ammunition. Someone has developed a .22 caliber round that shouldn't exist.
A training academy's entire stock of NL-22s is stolen overnight. The weapons are nearly worthless — so what does someone need fifty training pistols for?

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, almost toy-like semi-automatic pistol with clean lines and a deliberately approachable aesthetic. The silhouette is classic and unadorned—a full-size training platform that looks more like precision sporting equipment than a weapon. Its proportions feel intentionally friendly, lacking the aggressive cant or tactical protrusions of duty weapons.
physical_description.dimensions: 19 cm overall length, 12 cm grip height, 3.2 cm slide width. Barrel length: 10.2 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Remarkably light in hand—0.38 kg feels almost insubstantial, almost plastic-toy-light. Perfectly balanced for extended training sessions, with no muzzle-heavy feel. Recoil impulse is barely perceptible.
physical_description.primary_material: Lightweight reinforced polymer frame with steel slide and barrel. Internal components are hardened steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal-gray polymer with brushed stainless steel slide. Deliberately unmarred and clean, giving it a medical or educational device appearance rather than combat aesthetic.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray frame with brushed silver slide. Minimal accent colors—perhaps muted teal or navy safety indicators.
physical_description.grip_texture: Lightly textured polymer grip with gentle stippling pattern. Ergonomic finger grooves. Not aggressive or tactical—more like high-end sporting equipment. Slightly warm to the touch.
distinctive_features: Minimal control levers—simplified safety and slide release for new shooters
Magazine well with subtle witness holes showing round count
Crisp, easy-to-read sights—three-dot tritium setup in muted colors
Lightening cuts in frame visible through semi-translucent polymer
Recessed serial plate on left frame, deliberately small and unobtrusive
Extremely short trigger reset and take-up for accuracy training
Very slight forward serrations on slide—more aesthetic than functional
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Small 'NKOMO-LINDQVIST' text embossed on left frame in clean sans-serif font. 'NL-22 PEACEMAKER' engraved on right side of slide in italics. Serial number plate is recessed and modest. South African and Scandinavian small-print compliance markings on grip.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or near-pristine—maintained like training equipment rather than field gear. Occasional use scratches on frame from range bag contact, but generally unblemished. The weapon looks educational, not battle-tested.
